newsitem.title: USA: Oil drillers continue strong, rates firm. [CORRECTED 18:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Oil drillers continue strong, rates firm. [CORRECTED 18:45 GMT]

text.p: Oil drilling and service stocks continued firm on optimism over positive earnings surprises and strength in contract rates.

Yesterday, Reading & Bates Corp was awarded a five year contract by Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Shell Deepwater Development Inc for a deepwater semisubmersible rig to operate in the Gulf of Mexico, which will provide revenues of $335 million against a projected construction cost of $235 million, with delivery scheduled for 2000.

"This is a good return on capital and it is a positive sign for the sector that Shell is signalling it is looking at a seven and a half year view from now," said Iain Smith, analyst at Rodman & Renshaw.
Reading & Bates shares added 3/4 to 28-5/8 in late morning trade, continuing a week long rally.

"These stocks are now back where they were in January, but commodity prices are down 25 percent; perhaps investors have finally woken up to realize that these stocks have decoupled from the oil price," said Smith.
He noted that the sector could provide some positive earnings surprises and investors looking for earnings momentum are looking at the drilling sector rather than technology stocks.
"You can still pick up Transocean Offshore (Inc ) for 12 (corrects from 6.15) times next year's earnings, which is not even the market multiple," Smith said.
Marine Drilling Cos Inc continued yesterday's rally on the back of a contract worth $164-188 million.
The stock was up 1-3/16 at 23-5/16. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
